blocks.heading: Cost-benefit analysis
blocks.text: Cost-benefit analysis is the valuation by a government agency of social and private costs and benefits resulting from a decision. Here the treatment is descriptive: identify the likely positive and negative effects, who bears or receives them, alternatives and important uncertainties. A business profit forecast covers only part of that wider assessment. A severe lasting effect may matter even when another benefit is easier to count. Avoid pretending that a list of benefits on one side automatically outweighs fewer but more serious harms.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A road-linked workshop proposal offers business income and improved shared access but also construction disruption. The assessment should consider the firm’s costs and returns, users’ access benefit and neighbours’ disruption. It needs evidence about scale and duration rather than merely counting statements.
